chapter: Jelly Roll's road trip, Benny Carter and Chick Webb
title: A year and a half with Chick Webb, before the commercial turn
summary: Procope was with Webb into 1931; the band was a local stomping jazz band at the Savoy, becoming commercial only later with Ella Fitzgerald.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So the Chick Webb date, that was just a brief thing? No. You were with Chick Webb for awhile, weren't you?
Oh, of course, yes. I was with Chick for about a year and a half, something like that. Just about a year and a half.
Yeah, that's right. Yeah, into '31. And I went from Chick to Fletcher Henderson.
Now, at that point the Chick Webb band hadn't really become a very popular band.
I mean that hit later on.

No, no, no, no. Chick had a good go at the Savoy Ballroom and around New York, you know, sort of -- well, it was more local, like up and down the east coast, like we'd go down to Baltimore and play a dance once in awhile or Washington and play a dance. And Atlantic City, you know,

within hailing distance of New York, where you could go down and come back, you know. Then another time we got -- Chick's home was in Baltimore and one summer we went to Baltimore and played all that area around there, you know. But that's as far as he got at that time.
I was trying to think of that -- it just escapes me now -- the name of the flute player.
Wayman Carver, yes. Was he with --
Oh, no, no, no, no, no, no. He came in the band when Chick -- Chick turned commercial, you know.

And he -- well, he had the knack -- it's a funny thing, he had the knack of knowing what to do with a band. He knew the people to get. So at the time, when Ella, Ella Fitzgerald came, he had -- he knew how to adjust to the commercial aspect, because he had to play her arrangements, which was the important thing then. But before that, when I was with him, the important thing was just playing stomping, knockdown jazz, and that was it. The more jazz we played the better, and of course at the Savoy you got all the chance you wanted to play just jazz, and that's all we played.
